The graph of f(x)f(x)f(x) from x=0x=0x=0 to x=4x=4x=4 forms a triangle with a base of 4 units (from 0 to 4 on the x-axis) and a height of 6 units (the value of f(x)f(x)f(x) at x=0x=0x=0). The area of a triangle is given by 12×base×height\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}21​×base×height. Therefore, the area is 12×4×6=12\frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 6 = 1221​×4×6=12.

The graph of the function f(x)=x2−4x+3f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 3f(x)=x2−4x+3 is shown below. What is the value of the definite integral ∫14f(x) dx\int_{1}^{4} f(x) \, dx∫14​f(x)dx?
A. 999
B. 000
C. 121212
D. −9-9−9
Correct Answer: (B) — 000
The problem asks for the definite integral of the function f(x)=x2−4x+3f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 3f(x)=x2−4x+3 from x=1x=1x=1 to x=4x=4x=4. We can find the antiderivative of f(x)f(x)f(x) and then apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.

The antiderivative of f(x)=x2−4x+3f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 3f(x)=x2−4x+3 is F(x)=x33−2x2+3x+CF(x) = \frac{x^3}{3} - 2x^2 + 3x + CF(x)=3x3​−2x2+3x+C.

Now, we evaluate F(x)F(x)F(x) at the limits of integration:

∫14(x2−4x+3) dx=[x33−2x2+3x]14\int_{1}^{4} (x^2 - 4x + 3) \, dx = \left[ \frac{x^3}{3} - 2x^2 + 3x \right]_{1}^{4}∫14​(x2−4x+3)dx=[3x3​−2x2+3x]14​

=(433−2(42)+3(4))−(133−2(12)+3(1))= \left( \frac{4^3}{3} - 2(4^2) + 3(4) \right) - \left( \frac{1^3}{3} - 2(1^2) + 3(1) \right)=(343​−2(42)+3(4))−(313​−2(12)+3(1))

=(643−2(16)+12)−(13−2+3)= \left( \frac{64}{3} - 2(16) + 12 \right) - \left( \frac{1}{3} - 2 + 3 \right)=(364​−2(16)+12)−(31​−2+3)

=(643−32+12)−(13+1)= \left( \frac{64}{3} - 32 + 12 \right) - \left( \frac{1}{3} + 1 \right)=(364​−32+12)−(31​+1)

=(643−20)−(13+1)= \left( \frac{64}{3} - 20 \right) - \left( \frac{1}{3} + 1 \right)=(364​−20)−(31​+1)

=643−20−13−1= \frac{64}{3} - 20 - \frac{1}{3} - 1=364​−20−31​−1

=(643−13)−(20+1)= \left( \frac{64}{3} - \frac{1}{3} \right) - (20 + 1)=(364​−31​)−(20+1)

=633−21= \frac{63}{3} - 21=363​−21

=21−21= 21 - 21=21−21

=0= 0=0

Therefore, the value of the definite integral is 0.

We are given that the equation of the tangent line at x=cx = cx=c is y−f(c)=12(x−c)y - f(c) = \frac{1}{2}(x - c)y−f(c)=21​(x−c). Comparing this to the general form, we see that f′(c)=12f'(c) = \frac{1}{2}f′(c)=21​. We are also given that f(c)=3f(c) = 3f(c)=3.
